news.t: Wales hungry to show they are not one-hit wonders
news.sum: Wales must kick on when they host Australia in the Nations Championship on Saturday, fresh from making history against New Zealand.

news.t: Bath score seven tries in Prem Cup win at Bristol
news.sum: Bath score seven tries to beat Bristol 39-14 at Ashton Gate for their second win in this season's Prem Rugby Cup.

news.t: Ireland XV ease to nine-try victory over Fiji Latui
news.sum: Ireland XV eased to a nine-try victory over Fijian Latui after a scarcely believable contest at Virgin Media Park.

news.t: Wales players gaining confidence in Prem - Williams
news.sum: Exposure to the English Prem has boosted the confidence of Wales' players, says scrum-half Tomos Williams.

news.t: South Africa continue to lament Prendergast decision
news.sum: South Africa assistant coach Mzwandile Stick declared "no one is going to break us" as he backed under-fire head coach Rassie Erasmus and criticised the decision to clear Ireland's Sam Prendergast to play.

news.t: Stacked England aim to pile on style and add to All Black misery
news.sum: England's easy-on-the-eye revival will be stress-tested by a New Zealand side under sudden pressure on Saturday

news.t: Glos-Hartpury aim to name new head coach in January
news.sum: Gloucester-Hartpury will not appoint a new head coach until January, says the club's commercial sales director James Forrester.

news.t: 'No-one is going to break us' - defiant Boks face Ireland without Erasmus
news.sum: South Africa prepare to face Ireland in a much-anticipated Nations Championship Test in Dublin without banned head coach Rassie Erasmus.

news.t: Preview: War of words tees up fiery Aviva Test
news.sum: After five days of press conferences and disciplinary matters, of hip-drops and knee-drops, we have a game of rugby to cover, writes Neil Treacy.

news.t: Irish scrum set for defining test against the Springboks
news.sum: Twelve months on from Ireland's scrum being destroyed by South Africa, this week will show what improvements have been made, writes Neil Treacy.

news.t: McDowall goes from farm hand to Scotland captain as Darge injured
news.sum: Stafford McDowall was working on his dad's farm when he got the call to play for Scotland against Australia on Sunday - and six days later will be captain against Japan after Rory Darge suffered a late injury blow.

news.t: Cornish Pirates prop Petch banned for dangerous tackle
news.sum: Cornish Pirates prop Alfie Petch is banned for up to three matches for a dangerous tackle.

news.t: Clarkson replaces Illo on Irish bench to face Springboks
news.sum: South Africa have been forced into a change to their second row for Saturday's Nations Championship clash against Ireland in Dublin with Franco Mostert replacing Ruan Nortje.

news.t: Huge challenge for 'Roy of the Rovers' Sheehan - Lenihan
news.sum: Donal Lenihan says Ireland's "Roy of the Rovers" Dan Sheehan will shoulder a huge responsibility against South Africa at Aviva Stadium tomorrow after being picked to start at number 8.

news.t: PWR title, England recall, Lions tour - ambitious Atkin-Davies returns
news.sum: England and Bristol hooker Lark Atkin-Davies on her aims of winning a PWR title and making the Lions tour as she returns to the sport a new mum.

news.t: Refereeing is tough and coaches should 'protect the game' - Farrell
news.sum: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell says refereeing in rugby is "never going to be perfect" because it is such a complex sport.

news.t: Flanker Tizzano looks forward to Morgan reunion
news.sum: After their controversial 2025 Lions incident, Australia flanker Carlo Tizzano is looking forward to meeting Wales' Jac Morgan in Cardiff.

news.t: 'Clearer' approach has lifted England mood - Itoje
news.sum: Captain Maro Itoje says a clearer sense of purpose and unity has coincided with improved performances from England this autumn.

news.t: Gloucester-Hartpury boss Murphy exits on eve of new season
news.sum: Gloucester-Hartpury head of rugby Dan Murphy leaves the club on the eve of the new Premiership Women's Rugby season.

news.t: 'It's one of the hardest sports in the world to referee'
news.sum: It's been a week like no other ahead of an Ireland international, and as Andy Farrell sat down to address the media yesterday after naming his team to face South Africa, it was hard to know where to start.

news.t: Farrell backs 'world class' Sheehan to make back row mark
news.sum: Andy Farrell is backing Dan Sheehan to take his move into the back row "in his stride" ahead of Saturday's meeting with South Africa.

news.t: Saracens prop Street signs new two-year deal
news.sum: Tighthead prop Marcus Street extends his stay at Prem side Saracens.

news.t: Furbank leads returning England trio for All Blacks visit
news.sum: England are boosted by the recovery and return of George Furbank, Seb Atkinson and Ollie Chessum to face New Zealand

news.t: Sheehan named at number 8 for Ireland's Springboks clash
news.sum: Dan Sheehan has been picked to start at number 8 for Ireland in Saturday's meeting with South Africa, with head coach Andy Farrell taking a bold approach to the Nations Championship clash with the world champions.

news.t: Ireland hooker Sheehan at number eight for Springboks game
news.sum: Ireland captain Dan Sheehan is named at number eight for Saturday's highly anticipated Nations Championship match against world champions South Africa in Dublin.

news.t: Van der Flier: 'These are the games you want to play in'
news.sum: Josh van der Flier admits Ireland will have to get "everything" right if they are to turn over the world champions South Africa in Dublin on Saturday.

news.t: Botham 'disappointed' to be rested after starring against All Blacks
news.sum: Wales opt to freshen up their back row to face Australia with James Botham missing out despite his heroics against New Zealand.

news.t: Wainwright and Adams back for Wales against Australia
news.sum: Wales make four changes to their starting line-up that beat the All Blacks for the Nations Championship meeting with Australia.

news.t: Erasmus 'not dominating the coffee room' - Timoney
news.sum: Ireland back row Nick Timoney says players are "not living under a rock" but any talk of Rassie Erasmus' six-game ban is not dominating their conversations.

news.t: Could England fears lead to fewer overseas players in PWR?
news.sum: The RFU wants PWR to protect the interests of England's Red Roses, which could see a reduction in the number of international players in the league.

news.t: Boks focusing on rugby as Rassie sets up viewing party
news.sum: Expect the TV viewing figures to be off the chart on Saturday evening when Ireland and the Springboks finally face off at Aviva Stadium.

news.t: Ireland v South Africa: All You Need to Know
news.sum: Here's everything you need to know ahead of Ireland's final home game of 2026 against the world champions South Africa.

news.t: McCarthy to captain Ireland XV in Fijian clash
news.sum: Leinster hooker Gus McCarthy and Ulster back-row David McCann have both returned from senior camp to start for the Ireland XV squad when they take on Fijian Latui on Friday night in Virgin Media Park (7.45pm).

news.t: Divide and conquer - now maverick Erasmus plans online watchalong
news.sum: Rassie Erasmus is a serial offender when it comes to criticising officials, but he retains huge support in South Africa - and has unique plans for following his team's game against Ireland.

news.t: Rassie banned, Prendergast free as Boks rivalry heats up
news.sum: Neil Treacy is joined by Hugh Hogan and Johne Murphy on a jam-packed RTÉ Rugby podcast ahead of Ireland and South Africa's Nations Championship clash on Saturday.

news.t: SA Rugby condemns online abuse of World Rugby officials
news.sum: South African Rugby has condemned online abuse of World Rugby officials in the wake of the team's weekend defeat to France, and subsequent punishment handed out to coach Rassie Erasmus.

news.t: Ireland fly-half Prendergast cleared to face South Africa
news.sum: Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast successfully appeals against citing to make himself available to face South Africa on Saturday.

news.t: Prendergast free to play South Africa as citing dismissed
news.sum: Sam Prendergast will be available for selection for Saturday's Nations Championship clash with South Africa after the citing against him was dismissed.

news.t: Lancaster agrees contract extension with Connacht
news.sum: Stuart Lancaster has signed a two-year contract extension that will keep him at Connacht until the end of the 2028/2029 season.

news.t: Frawley repaying the faith as Springboks rematch looms
news.sum: The last time Ireland defeated South Africa, Ciarán Frawley was the man of the hour. Now, after a strong start to the season with Connacht, he looks set to play a major role in the latest test between the nations.

news.t: Erasmus handed six-match suspension over comments
news.sum: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been suspended for six international matches by World Rugby, starting with this Saturday's Nations Championship clash with Ireland at Aviva Stadium.

news.t: South Africa head coach Erasmus banned for six matches
news.sum: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been banned for six matches by World Rugby over comments he made about match officials.

news.t: 'Is that not match-fixing?' - South Africa's Erasmus questions officiating
news.sum: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus predicts Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast will not face a ban after being cited, and questions standards in officiating.

news.t: Laws remain headline act despite weekend of excitement
news.sum: Another week of international rugby matches has brought yet another distraction and focus on the laws rather than the quality of rugby on display, writes Jonny Holland.

news.t: Lenihan: Rassie Erasmus knows what he's doing
news.sum: Donal Lenihan says that Ireland should have the depth to deal with a big absence less than a year out from the World Cup.

news.t: Erasmus makes extraordinary double-standard claims
news.sum: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus says he believes Sam Prendergast will be free to take on the Springboks this Saturday, suggesting the out-half will escape a suspension for an alleged hip-drop tackle due to a "tech

news.t: Explosive Erasmus comments set the tone for Test week
news.sum: By naming his team and holding a press conference on Monday, it was always likely that Rassie Erasmus would set the narrative of the week before the meeting of Ireland and South Africa on Saturday.

news.t: Nations Championship final round - who needs what?
news.sum: Who needs what to qualify for the inaugural Nations Championship final on 29 November?

news.t: Rugby Union Weekly
news.sum: Gabriel Hamer-Webb joins Danny, Ashy and Chris after Wales stunned the All Blacks.

news.t: Etzebeth returns as Boks change five for Ireland showdown
news.sum: South Africa have recalled experienced lock Eben Etzebeth for their crunch Nations Championship test against Ireland in Dublin on Saturday, one of five changes to the starting XV that lost to France in Paris.

news.t: SA recall Etzebeth as Erasmus defends late changes
news.sum: South Africa record cap holder Eben Etzebeth is recalled for Saturday's much-anticipated Nations Championship game against Ireland in Dublin.

news.t: Prendergast cited and could miss South Africa game
news.sum: Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast is in danger of missing Saturday's Nations Championship match against South Africa after being cited for a tackle against Fiji.

news.t: Ireland sweating on Prendergast after out-half is cited
news.sum: Ireland could be without Sam Prendergast for Saturday's crucial Nations Championship clash with South Africa, after the out-half was cited for an alleged hip-drop tackle in the 43-15 win against Fiji.

news.t: Sheehan on track for Springboks but Osborne injured
news.sum: Ireland are confident captain Dan Sheehan will be fit for Saturday's crucial meeting with South Africa at Aviva Stadium, while Jamie Osborne has been ruled out as expected after suffering a pectoral injury last weekend.

news.t: 'We know we can do it' - Farrell eyes Springbok scalp
news.sum: Head coach Andy Farrell says Ireland will look to draw inspiration from the big wins they have had under his watch when they renew their rivalry with world champions South Africa this weekend.

news.t: Scotland win hard fought match against Australia
news.sum: Scotland eked out a hard-fought home 15-12 win over Australia but were unable to get the bonus point they craved in a Nations Championship match that failed to catch fire.

news.t: Baloucoune: 'Kick in the arse' will prepare us for Boks
news.sum: If the weekend gone by showed us anything, it's that the Nations Championship is bursting with competitive matchups, meaning the gap between wins and losses is never more than a deep breath away.

news.t: Farrell: 'We know all about them, they know all about us'
news.sum: Andy Farrell says he has full belief his side can topple the world champions on Saturday, when they renew what has become an epic rivalry with South Africa.

news.t: Ireland must improve on 'clunky' display for Boks
news.sum: Tommy O'Brien feels Ireland must improve on the "clunky" win over Fiji on Saturday when they face world champions South Africa on Saturday.

news.t: Irish scrum improving but true test awaits vs the Boks
news.sum: While Ireland's scrum has been dominant in the first two games of this Nations Championship window, the true test of Ireland's setpiece is in store next week.
